Abstract: This paper proposes a digital twin model based on dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) for the electro-optical system for its performance monitoring. In this model, a system-level performance indicator from the perspective of the energy domain using Modulation Transfer Function (MTF) is first developed, which avoids tedious modeling of performance interactions between the multiple subsystems of the electro-optical system. Then, a DBN is constructed from the evolution of MTF to denote the dynamic performance degradation process and the propagation of epistemic uncertainty. In order to make the digital twin model capable of tracking and predicting the system performance states, an improved Gaussian particle filter with kernel smoothing (GPF-KS) is proposed as the inference algorithm for DBN. A real dataset collected in the laboratory environment is used to validate the feasibility of the digital twin model and verify the effectiveness of the GPF-KS inference algorithm. The results show that our method is effective for joint estimation of states and parameters, leading to reliable estimation and prediction of the electro-optical system on-line health-status.

Abstract: Industrial digital twins must continuously ingest online data during long-term operation and revise the virtual-to-physical mapping under non-stationary factors such as operating-condition switching, equipment degradation, and observation bias. To address these issues, this paper proposes Dynamic Hierarchical Posterior Evolution (DHPE) for non-stationary industrial digital twins. In the representation layer, a hierarchical Gaussian-Inv-Gamma formulation with dynamic scale adjustment is introduced to maintain uncertainty health during online updating. In the evolution layer, complex posteriors are projected into Gaussian-mixture interface posteriors, and geometric Wasserstein distance is used to jointly incorporate historical posterior inheritance and physically anchored priors, thereby enabling smooth recursion under non-Gaussian conditions while preserving long-term physical consistency. A closed-loop mechanism integrating drift monitoring, state switching, and geometric feedback is further constructed to adaptively regulate inheritance strength, anchoring stiffness, and uncertainty width. Online experiments on titanium reduction furnace temperature prediction under three representative non-stationary scenarios show that DHPE delivers more stable error trajectories, more reasonable interval coverage, and more consistent probabilistic predictions, while maintaining strong posterior recovery capability and long-term robustness.

Abstract: This article presents a short-term (1-h ahead) physics-guided multirepresentation feature fusion framework for photovoltaic (PV) power prediction with uncertainty quantification based on quantile regression for interval forecasting. The DT residual, computed causally using only training data, is incorporated as a physics-informed feature to capture unmodeled nonlinearities. PIs are learned using the pinball (quantile) loss function, replacing heuristic assumptions, and feature-representation fusion reduces uncertainty while enhancing robustness. Validation on real meteorological datasets from Izki and Manah stations (2017–2023) shows that conventional feature sets achieve root mean squared error (RMSE) values between 0.14–0.17 with coefficient of determination ($R^{2}$) ranging from 0.47–0.61. Using DT residual features, LSTM and GRU achieve $R^{2} > 0.998$ with RMSE $\approx 0.042$, while RF reaches $R^{2} = 0.897$ and a relatively higher RMSE $\approx 0.326$. In summary, the framework offers a reproducible, physically grounded, and uncertainty-aware solution for next-generation solar energy forecasting, explicitly quantifying prediction uncertainty and leveraging physics-informed residuals to enhance predictive reliability and interpretability across both real and synthetic scenarios.

Abstract: The traditional Bayesian approach for model calibrations is based on the random theory, while it needs a great amount of information to construct precise probability distributions of observed data. In this approach, the observed data are described as random variables that obey certain probability distributions, while some of their distribution parameters are given variation intervals rather than precise values. Because of the existing interval parameters, a probability density distribution strip is formed in the posterior space, instead of a single distribution for each unknown model parameter as we usually obtain in the traditional Bayesian calibration. As an example, in this study, a thermal model calibration problem is investigated to demonstrate the effectiveness of the present approach.

Abstract: The current trend in robotics is to enhance robustness against uncertainties through complex modern control methods, applied to either single- or multi-agent systems. With constant improvement of the Internet of Things, real-time systems needed different software architectures and communication systems to enable their remote operation, with the same degree of flexibility when operating the systems in-situ. Abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) and agent-based approaches to support intelligent and autonomous urban systems. This systematic literature review (SLR) analyzes 82 primary research studies describing AI-driven agent-based approaches in urban digital twins as a system of systems and found in four major scientific databases, i.e. IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, and ACM Digital Library. The selected studies were systematically examined with respect to digital twin types, AI techniques used, agent type, agent roles, maturity level, application domains, and key challenges. We also identified that most studies remain at relatively low Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) and rely predominantly on simulation-based or conceptual validation, revealing a substantial gap between technological advancement and real-world deployment. The analysis further shows that implementation challenges evolve across the DT life-cycle. Moreover, we found that only a limited proportion of studies explicitly address uncertainty, while the majority rely on deterministic or idealized assumptions. Our analysis further revealed that most urban digital twin systems are in the early stages of development, and we identified key research gaps and, based on this, suggested future research directions.
